title: Edge reset before return-A learning and topographic error
hypothesis: Clearing the Hebbian edge set immediately before return-A learning reduces the prior-A arm's mean return-A topographic error relative to retaining those edges, with prototype positions, node counts, other learning state, and the subsequent return samples identical inside every pair. The unchanged engine refuses a cleared graph, so a recorded isolated-node relaxation and every capacity, insertion, and node-removal count are prerequisites for reading the difference as an edge effect; a real capacity or removal deviation forbids a capacity-isolated claim.
